claims.statement: Talon selects durable history storage from DEEPAGENTS_TALON_HISTORY_URI, defaults to SQLite at the checkpoint path, supports SQLite, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, or exactly one entry-point plugin for another scheme, and namespaces its archive by assistant ID.

Talon StoreRecords provides recoverable, bounded mutations for one active in-process archive writer: it serializes access with a lock, recovers a prior journal before access, writes a redo journal before idempotent batch operations, and clears that journal only after successful recovery.

Talon's StoreConversationArchive keeps transcript metadata and optional vector indexing on separate store instances, recovers records before use, waits for vector work on close, and binds each session to its trusted chat scope so a session cannot be appended from another scope or while deleting.

Talon creates a per-assistant home under the configured base directory, validates assistant IDs to prevent unsafe path components, applies mode 0700 to the home and its state directories, and verifies that state paths remain directly inside that home.

Talon persists model selections in models.json, active conversation generations in conversations.json, and assistant-scoped cron jobs in cron/jobs.json; cron job records include the origin conversation/channel and run status fields.

ConversationSaver persists a graph checkpoint before appending its message revisions to the independent archive and acknowledging the archive checkpoint; there is no cross-store transaction, archive failures propagate for repair, and idempotent archive revisions avoid duplicates on retry.

ConversationSaver shields checkpoint/archive writes from cancellation until both finish, then re-raises cancellation, while its shared lock prevents reset or deletion from racing an incomplete append.

Only root graph checkpoints with trusted Talon channel/chat metadata are eligible for transcript archival; unscoped and nested graph writes are excluded, and archive session registration prevents a session from being reassigned across chat scopes.
Talon validates history URI syntax and converts metadata-store, plugin, and archive startup failures into generalized configuration errors so connection URI credentials are not exposed.

History vector indexes are separate from archive metadata, selected independently per storage scheme or exactly one vector plugin, and guarded by an embedding fingerprint; an incompatible retained index requires explicit reindexing that preserves transcripts and resumes progress after interruption.

Scheduled runs use their own cron thread checkpoints and may read the origin chat's scoped history, but their graph writes are archive read-only and deletion is disallowed; a final result successfully delivered to the chat can still be recorded in its archive.

Talon publishes cron records by fsyncing and mode-0600-replacing a temporary JSON file, while live CronJobStore instances sharing a resolved path serialize reads and complete mutations with one reentrant in-process lock; other processes and external writers are not coordinated, so each cron file has one owning process.

The Talon README describes Talon as experimental, not intended for production or enterprise use, and lacking production-grade multi-tenant security boundaries; channel access should be treated as access to the operator's agent, credentials, tools, and local host resources.
For a configured model host, Talon opens the URI-selected checkpointer and history archive as async contexts, then supplies the agent a ConversationSaver wrapping both.
Conversation deletion is scope-limited and protects active or running sessions; deletion may be partially completed and retried using the same session IDs.
Archive retrieval bounds pages to 20 items and scans to 500 records, raising an error rather than silently returning a complete-looking result after the scan limit is exceeded.
Talon records a final reply for semantic-history eligibility only after the host reports successful non-silent delivery; failures to record that history are logged without changing the send result.

DEEPAGENTS_TALON_CHECKPOINT_URI selects built-in SQLite/file, PostgreSQL, or MongoDB checkpointers, or exactly one checkpoint-backend entry-point plugin; checkpointer initialization errors are sanitized into configuration errors to avoid exposing URI credentials.

Checkpoint backend selection is independent from history backend selection; the default checkpointer is the assistant-local SQLite path, whereas remote checkpoint thread IDs are not automatically namespaced by assistant ID and changing the URI does not migrate checkpoint data.

DeepAgents uses a DeltaChannel for the messages state with snapshots every 50 updates; its reducer relies on LangGraph-assigned stable message IDs and deterministically replaces, removes, or resets messages during replay.

StateBackend is a thread-scoped virtual filesystem in LangGraph state: it reads fresh channel state and queues partial files-channel updates through LangGraph config keys, so writes are available in the current superstep and persist only with the graph's checkpoints.

StoreBackend stores file records in a caller-selected BaseStore namespace, persists across threads that share that namespace, and validates namespace components to prevent wildcard or glob injection; it may obtain the store from graph execution context or use an explicitly supplied store.
